title: Wire ISO post: AWT requires a tip-disposal code, and the end sequence can write more than three M-code blocks in a row

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

- The wire ISO post refuses each machine file that sets `edm.awt: true` and has no `edm.codes.tip_disposal`. Many wire controls thread and cut with two codes and have no separate tip-disposal code. The post then refuses a legal program.
- At the end of a section and of the program, the post can write these blocks in sequence: `taper_off`, `cut`, `tip_disposal`, `M00` or `M01`, `M30`. Each of these can be an M-code block with no G code. The GF AgieCharmilles ISO programming manual does not permit more than three consecutive M-code blocks with no G code, so the control stops with an alarm.

## Expected

- `tip_disposal` is optional when `awt` is true. The post writes it only when the machine file states it.
- The post does not write more than three M-code blocks in a row. For example, it writes the stop and `M30` so that no fourth M-only block follows.

## Evidence (upstream main `eafe6aec6`)

- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:55`, `:150-164`: `AWT_REQUIRED` and the refusal.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:456-470`: the section end.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:493-496`: `onClose` writes `M30`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_slug_punch.nc`: the program ends with the cut code, the tip-out code and `M30`.

Workarounds: put a comment in `edm.codes.tip_disposal`, and remove the stop before the program end.

Found by the post audit against the GF AgieCharmilles manuals (#4130).

## Done means

- An AWT machine file with no `tip_disposal` posts.
- A golden pins the end sequence with a stop and shows no more than three M-code blocks in a row.
